title: WHAT IF YOU COULD GLIMPSE ONE MINUTE AHEAD?

segments.line: It's mum. You let it ring.
What if you could glimpse one minute ahead?
Sounds amazing. Honestly, it does. You
But here's the catch. A glimpse isn't free.
Your brain is two percent of your body weight, and
it burns a fifth of all your energy.
Twenty watts, nonstop. About a dim light bulb.
Now run a whole minute of life in one second. Every single time you glimpse.
Twelve hundred watts. A space heater, running inside your skull.
At first, a headache. A dull, pounding one.
Then the world stutters. Like a video that won't load.
Then the glimpses won't stop. One after another after another.
Your head is hot. Your vision is white. Your ears are ringing.
So what happens when the power fails?

Pip catches the bus door, hauls himself on; the bus lurches forward

Mo's mouth opens, Pip's voice comes out first; both freeze, staring
the phone buzzes on the desk, MUM calling
Pip's eyes, a cyan box round the call to come, the future holds
